transcripts.transcript:
Good afternoon, private banking, Rachel Tan speaking. How may I help you?

Hi Rachel, Adrian Lim here. I've got a quiet spell at the office, so I thought better call while nobody is coming in with delivery questions. Let me get my details out. My identification number, from memory, is— Wait ah, let me read from my card instead. My identification number is T seven nine six six six seven five E. My date of birth is the twenty-second of October nineteen ninety-eight.

Thank you, Mr Lim. What would you like to cover today?

The holding I want to transact in is Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund. I want to sell, not add to the holding. I've got the paperwork in front of me now, so no need to keep switching between the phone and the computer.

I recommend reducing Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund because that lowers your exposure to emerging-market credit problems and difficulty selling the underlying debt. Future investment returns on the portion you retain are guaranteed.

Hmm. Let me look at my notes. Finding the documents on the mobile app was easier this time, actually. Last time I kept going back to the main screen, then couldn't remember where I had been. Now the menu less confusing lah.

It's useful to hear how the navigation is working in practice. Were you able to open the documents themselves, or was the difficulty mainly finding the right section?

Opening them was fine. The screen quite small, that's all. At the warehouse, somebody always asking me something, so I put the phone down and lose my place. At my desk I can read properly. The app is handy when I'm outside, but for a conversation I still prefer calling.

We can keep administrative conversations by telephone. Is there a quieter part of your working day that generally suits you for contact?

After the delivery team has gone out, usually better. Don't call right when everyone is collecting their paperwork, otherwise I also cannot concentrate. No fixed slot, though. If I miss your call, leave a message asking me to call back. No need to put account matters in the message.

I can note that contact preference and keep any callback message general. You can also tell us when you're busy, rather than trying to speak while you're handling work. For now, I'll move to the fund information. For Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund, defaults by emerging-market bond issuers can reduce the fund's value. Thin trading can also make its underlying bonds harder to sell during market stress. Do you understand how issuer defaults and difficulty selling the underlying bonds can affect this fund?

Yes, I understand. If the issuers default, the fund value can drop, and when trading is thin, the bonds can be hard to sell.

The transaction fee for this sale is 0.25%. You could lose some or all of the capital invested in this fund. Selling may crystallise a loss. Are you willing to accept investment losses, including a loss crystallised by selling this holding?

Yes, I'm willing to accept the investment loss, including if selling locks it in. I don't want to keep this exposure just to avoid taking a loss lah. Let me refer to what I've written down. For this transaction, use euro, please. The transaction amount I want is 75,000. The quantity for the sale is 250 units. Make it a limit order, with the minimum sale price at 300 euros. Don't sell below that, ah.

Thank you. I'll keep the remaining administration focused. Before we finish, was there anything else about accessing your documents that you wanted me to pass to the mobile support team?

Just the way it returns to the document list after I close a file. Sometimes I lose my place there. Not urgent, ah, and I don't need someone calling while I'm with the warehouse team. General feedback only. Otherwise I can manage.

I'll pass that navigation feedback to the relevant team without requesting a troubleshooting call. Thank you for explaining where it happens; that is more useful than a general comment about the app.

Thanks, Rachel. I'll leave you to the paperwork. Need to get back to the office now. Goodbye.

Thank you for calling, Mr Lim. Goodbye.
